title: Understanding New UPI Rules: Impact on Insurance, SIPs, and AutoPay
description: New UPI rules effective October 15 introduce an interchange fee of 0.4% for merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000. This fee is primarily levied on Payment Sy.

faq.q: Is UPI AutoPay now more expensive?
faq.a: No, UPI AutoPay mandates for recurring payments like SIPs, insurance premiums, and subscription bills are explicitly exempt from the new 0.4% interchange fee. Your existing AutoPay setups will not incur additional charges.

faq.q: Will my SIP payments through UPI AutoPay be charged extra?
faq.a: No, SIP payments made via UPI AutoPay will not be charged extra. The new interchange fee does not apply to recurring payments set up through the AutoPay facility.

faq.q: Does this fee apply to all UPI transactions?
faq.a: No, the 0.4% interchange fee only applies to merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000. Person-to-person (P2P) transfers and all UPI AutoPay mandates remain free of this specific charge.

This fee is an interchange fee primarily paid by the acquiring bank (the merchant's bank) to the issuing bank (the customer's bank) and other Payment System Providers (PSPs) involved in facilitating the transaction. It is not a direct charge to the end consumer for most transactions.

faq.q: What if a merchant asks me to pay the fee directly?
faq.a: The interchange fee is an operational cost within the payment ecosystem. While merchants might adjust their pricing to account for such costs, directly asking a consumer to pay an additional "UPI fee" on top of the product/service price is not the intended mechanism of this interchange fee.

faq.q: How does this affect NRIs using UPI?
faq.a: For Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) using UPI, primarily for P2P transfers or specific merchant payments in India, the same rules apply. P2P transfers remain free, and UPI AutoPay for recurring payments will not incur the new fee. Only merchant transactions above ₹2,000 might involve the interchange fee for the ecosystem players.

faq.q: Where can I find the official notification for these changes?
faq.a: Official notifications and circulars regarding UPI framework changes are typically issued by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). You can find them on their respective official websites.
